description: Sol Keepers teaches kids the real trade-offs of surviving on the moon, using live NASA space weather and mission data to turn every decision into a lesson.
summary: We developed Junior Astronaut Trainer, an interactive, browser-based lunar outpost survival and mission-control simulation designed for children aged 7–12. The application addresses the challenge of translating complex deep-space mission planning into an engaging learning experience by placing players in charge of a multi-day lunar outpost where every decision involves a genuine engineering trade-off—such as dividing limited electrical power between life support, radiation shielding, food production, and communications. Rather than presenting space science as passive facts or consequence-free trivia, the game models compounding resource costs and cause-and-effect outcomes using plain, accessible language. This is important because it helps young learners intuitively understand how real astronauts and NASA mission planners balance human survival, radiation safety, and scientific objectives in extreme lunar environments.
details: Junior Astronaut Trainer is a single-page web application that simulates day-to-day resource management and crisis decision-making at a lunar habitat. Players monitor core mission systems—including electrical power, oxygen and water life support, radiation shielding, food production, and Earth communications—and must allocate limited reserves across simulated mission days. Because no choice is free, boosting one system—such as reinforcing radiation shielding ahead of a solar flare or powering hydroponic grow lights—reduces capacity elsewhere, creating authentic engineering trade-offs. Dynamic space weather hazards and communication delays challenge players to adapt their strategy, while built-in contextual explanations define key scientific concepts like radiation dose and closed-loop life support without overwhelming younger audiences. The primary goal of the tool is to promote replayable, hands-on STEM learning where students can experiment and learn from mission setbacks in an accessible browser environment that requires no downloads or accounts. Technically, the prototype is built using JavaScript (ES6+), React 19, HTML5, and CSS3, integrating D3-Geo and TopoJSON for interactive planetary and geographic map rendering inside a standalone HTML5 bundle.
